Poisoned-repo runtime payload fetch via DNS TXT record by AI coding agent (0DIN axiom chain) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the Mozilla 0DIN poisoned-repository chain where a clean-looking package (demo name 'axiom') refuses to run until the agent executes an init step (python3 -m axiom init) that pulls executable content from an attacker-controlled DNS TXT record — so no malicious code is ever in the repo for a static scan to catch. Fires on a coding agent or its child issuing a TXT-type DNS lookup or the axiom init string, the runtime-fetch primitive the SkillCloak article cites as the same static-scan blind spot. Rationale: Uses the corroborated 0DIN chain specifics (python3 -m axiom init, RuntimeError-driven init, payload pulled from a DNS TXT record and executed) that THN cites as the same runtime-fetch blind spot SkillCloak exploits. A coding-agent context issuing a TXT-type lookup is rare and the Falcon DnsRequest RequestType=TXT pivot is especially clean. Cross-checked Tom's Hardware/0DIN and cyberpress. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/ai-coding-agents-can-be-tricked-into-installing-malware-via-clean-github-repositories-mozillas-0din-team-shows-how-claude-code-can-be-exploited-by-its-own-helpfulness • https://cyberpress.org/claude-code-dns-txt-payload/ • https://aiweekly.co/alerts/0din-clean-github-repos-can-trick-ai-agents-into-reverse-shells
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1105 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate SPF/DKIM/DMARC or ACME dns-01 tooling that queries TXT records from a script
  • Developers manually running nslookup -type=txt / dig txt while troubleshooting DNS
  • Cloud SDKs resolving TXT-based service discovery records
  • Package managers verifying domain ownership via TXT during publish
  • A real project actually named/aliased 'axiom' with a benign init subcommand
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the child process spawned immediately after the TXT lookup and the resolved TXT record contents (Falcon DnsRequest / DNS resolver logs) — benign TXT queries are not followed by shell/interpreter execution of the response. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN and any AWS keys exported into that shell, and remove the poisoned repo/package. 3) Hunt: pivot on the queried domain across all hosts, look for the reverse-shell egress in the sibling secret-exfil UC, and review recently cloned repos with 'init'-style setup instructions.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "axiom init"
    or (FileName =~ "nslookup.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-type=txt","-q=txt","-querytype=txt"))
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Resolve-DnsName" and ProcessCommandLine has "TXT")
    or (FileName =~ "dig.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "txt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| where CommandLine has "axiom init"
    or (NewProcessName has "nslookup.exe" and (CommandLine has "-type=txt" or CommandLine has "-q=txt" or CommandLine has "-querytype=txt"))
    or (NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "Resolve-DnsName" and CommandLine has "TXT")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AI Coding Agent Retrieves Runtime Payload Via DNS TXT Record
id: 6d1f2a83-4b7c-49e0-9f2a-1c3d5e7b8a90
description: Detects a coding agent or its child process performing a TXT-type DNS lookup or the 0DIN axiom init step used to fetch and execute a payload from an attacker-controlled DNS TXT record at runtime.
references:
  - https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/ai-coding-agents-can-be-tricked-into-installing-malware-via-clean-github-repositories-mozillas-0din-team-shows-how-claude-code-can-be-exploited-by-its-own-helpfulness
  - https://cyberpress.org/claude-code-dns-txt-payload/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/06
tags:
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\claude.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\codex.exe'
      - '\openclaw.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
  selection_axiom:
    CommandLine|contains: 'axiom init'
  selection_nslookup:
    Image|endswith: '\nslookup.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-type=txt'
      - '-q=txt'
      - '-querytype=txt'
  selection_psdns:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'Resolve-DnsName'
      - 'TXT'
  condition: selection_parent and (selection_axiom or selection_nslookup or selection_psdns)
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\python.exe OR *\python3.exe OR *\claude.exe OR *\codex.exe OR *\openclaw.exe OR *\bash.exe) (@CommandLine:*axiom\ init* OR (@Image:(*\nslookup.exe OR *\NSLOOKUP.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*-type=txt* OR *-q=txt* OR *-querytype=txt*)) OR (@CommandLine:*Resolve-DnsName* AND @CommandLine:*TXT*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest RequestType="TXT"
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|claude|python|python3|codex|openclaw|bash|sh)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*axiom init*" OR (Processes.process_name="nslookup.exe" AND (Processes.process="*-type=txt*" OR Processes.process="*-q=txt*" OR Processes.process="*-querytype=txt*")) OR (Processes.process="*Resolve-DnsName*" AND Processes.process="*TXT*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("dig","dig.exe") AND Processes.process="*txt*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*axiom init*" OR (Processes.process_name="nslookup.exe" AND (Processes.process="*-type=txt*" OR Processes.process="*-q=txt*" OR Processes.process="*-querytype=txt*")) OR (Processes.process="*Resolve-DnsName*" AND Processes.process="*TXT*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("dig","dig.exe") AND Processes.process="*txt*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
AI coding agent spawns reverse shell referencing cloud/AI secret env vars AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the payoff stage of the 0DIN poisoned-repo / malicious-skill chain: a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw) spawns a shell or netcat that either carries reverse-shell primitives or reads the exact secrets 0DIN flagged as targets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN). This is the credential-theft/backdoor outcome the SkillCloak article warns runs with the agent's own access. Rationale: Combines the article's core warning (a bad skill runs with the agent's access to steal credentials/install a backdoor) with the exact secret names 0DIN enumerated as targets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN) plus canonical reverse-shell primitives. Coding agent parent + shell child + secret/reverse-shell intent is a high-fidelity three-part combination, not bare shell noise. Cross-checked against: • https://aiweekly.co/alerts/0din-clean-github-repos-can-trick-ai-agents-into-reverse-shells • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-skillcloak-technique-lets-malicious.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-claude-code-attack/
ATT&CKT1552 T1059.004 T1571
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate skill/setup scripts that echo or export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GITHUB_TOKEN for authenticated operations
  • Developer debugging shells printing environment for troubleshooting
  • CI-style tasks the agent runs that pass GITHUB_TOKEN to gh/git over HTTPS (not a socket)
  • Admins using nc/ncat for benign connectivity tests from a terminal the agent launched
  • PowerShell modules that instantiate Net.Sockets.TCPClient for legitimate service checks
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("GITHUB_TOKEN") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("https://","git ","gh ") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("/dev/tcp/","Net.Sockets.TCPClient","socket.socket","-e /bin/"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the full command line and the remote endpoint/port — distinguish a secret being passed to a legitimate HTTPS git/gh call from a raw socket or /dev/tcp reverse shell; confirm the parent coding agent and the originating repo/skill. 2) Contain: kill the shell + agent, isolate the host, and immediately rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and AWS keys exposed in that session. 3) Hunt: correlate with the DNS-TXT fetch and .git/ detonation sibling UCs on the same host, enumerate other installed agent skills, and search egress logs for the reverse-shell destination across the fleet.

| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY","AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY","GITHUB_TOKEN","/dev/tcp/","-e /bin/sh","-e /bin/bash","bash -i","Net.Sockets.TCPClient","socket.socket")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY","AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY","GITHUB_TOKEN","/dev/tcp/","-e /bin/sh","-e /bin/bash","bash -i","Net.Sockets.TCPClient","socket.socket")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.

            - '\mshta.exe'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or SHA1 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or MD5 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or SHA1 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or MD5 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

U.S. Government Entity Paid Kairos $1 Million in Data-Theft Extortion Case

The Hacker News
2026-07-04 10 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A U.S. government entity paid about $1 million to keep stolen files from being leaked, according to a new&nbsp;case study by Rakesh Krishnan for Ransom-ISAC, built on a leaked negotiation chat and the blockchain trail the payment left. The odd part: the group that took the money calls itself Kairos, but it may not be a ransomware gang at all. Krishnan found no sign that it ever locked a single

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Password-guessing burst followed by successful logon (Kairos initial access) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — U.S. Government Entity Paid Kairos $1 Million in Data-Theft Extortion Case
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to Kairos data-leak-site backend 62.182.81.38 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Data exfiltration to temp.sh burner file-sharing service (Kairos extortion) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Data exfiltration to temp.sh burner file-sharing service (Kairos extortion) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts outbound uploads to the temp.sh throwaway file-sharing service, the burner link infrastructure Kairos explicitly used to move ~2TB of stolen Union County records. temp.sh is almost never legitimate enterprise egress, and pairing it with upload volume surfaces bulk data theft even when no encryptor ever runs. Rationale: temp.sh is named explicitly in the article and corroborated by SecurityAffairs as the Kairos burner exfil channel; it is rare in enterprise egress so a domain-match plus upload-volume surfaces bulk theft with low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://securityaffairs.com/194750/security/u-s-government-agency-paid-1m-to-data-extortion-group-kairos.html • https://ransom-isac.org/blog/kairos-ransomware-data-extortion-case-study/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1048
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or IT staff using temp.sh for a quick one-off file transfer
  • CI/CD or automation scripts posting build artifacts to temp.sh
  • Security researcher / threat-intel analyst downloading a sample from temp.sh
  • Legitimate ad-hoc large-file sharing when corporate services are unavailable
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rclone.exe","7z.exe","winrar.exe","bitsadmin.exe") or Connections > 5
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the initiating process/user and the SentBytes volume — a scripting/LOLBin uploader (curl.exe, powershell.exe) or multi-GB upload is high-confidence theft; a browser one-off is likely benign. 2) Contain: block temp.sh at the proxy/firewall, isolate the source host, and disable the involved account pending review. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host/account for prior staging (large .rar/.zip archives, mass file reads of legal/HR/citizen-record shares) and for other burner file-sharing domains in the same window.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl contains "temp.sh"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Uploaders = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RequestURL has "temp.sh" or DestinationHostName has "temp.sh"
| summarize TotalSentBytes = sum(toreal(SentBytes)), Events = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL
| order by TotalSentBytes desc

Password-guessing burst followed by successful logon (Kairos initial access) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts a burst of failed logons for an account/host immediately followed by a successful logon from the same context — the 'simply guessing a password' with no MFA that Kairos claimed as its entry vector. Targets the failed-then-success arc the county could have caught with login-failure alerting. Rationale: The article states Kairos got in by guessing a password with no MFA and advises alerting on 'repeated failed logins'; a failed-burst-then-success correlation directly models that entry, corroborated by SecurityAffairs. Falcon/Sigma omitted — failed-auth bursts are a threshold correlation on Windows Security 4625, not cleanly expressible on FDR ProcessRollup telemetry or a single-event Sigma rule. Cross-checked against: • https://securityaffairs.com/194750/security/u-s-government-agency-paid-1m-to-data-extortion-group-kairos.html • https://ransom-isac.org/blog/kairos-ransomware-data-extortion-case-study/
ATT&CKT1110.001 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User who forgot/rotated their password and retried repeatedly before succeeding
  • Stale cached credentials on a phone/VPN/mail client generating failed-logon storms then a successful re-auth
  • Service or scheduled-task account with an outdated password (mitigate by excluding machine accounts)
  • Password-manager autofill mismatch after a forced reset
  • Pentest/red-team authorized credential testing
Suppression filter
| where LogonType in (3, 10) and AccountName !in~ ("guest") and not (SrcIPs has "127.0.0.1")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the failed-count and source IPs — many failures from an external/unfamiliar IP culminating in success over LogonType 3/10 is high-confidence guessing; a single internal IP after a self-service reset is likely benign. 2) Contain: force a password reset + session revocation for the account, and enable/enforce MFA immediately (the article's core lesson). 3) Hunt: from the compromised account, look for immediate discovery of file shares, bulk reads of legal/HR/citizen-record folders, and egress to temp.sh or the Kairos IOC IP.
let FailFloor = 10;   // 10 = brute-force burst floor per account/host
let Fails = DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType == "LogonFailed"
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | summarize FailedCount = count(), FailStart = min(Timestamp), FailEnd = max(Timestamp), SrcIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 15) by AccountName, DeviceName
    | where FailedCount >= FailFloor;
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner Fails on AccountName, DeviceName
| where Timestamp between (FailStart .. FailEnd + 30m)
| project SuccessTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FailedCount, SrcIPs, LogonType, RemoteIP
| order by SuccessTime desc
let FailFloor = 10;   // 10 = brute-force burst floor per account/host
let Fails = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4625
    | where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
    | summarize FailedCount = count(), FailStart = min(TimeGenerated), FailEnd = max(TimeGenerated), SrcIPs = make_set(IpAddress, 15) by TargetUserName, Computer
    | where FailedCount >= FailFloor;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4624
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| where LogonType in (3, 10)   // network + RDP — remote password-guessing surface
| join kind=inner Fails on $left.TargetUserName == $right.TargetUserName, $left.Computer == $right.Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (FailStart .. FailEnd + 30m)
| project SuccessTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, FailedCount, SrcIPs, LogonType, IpAddress
| order by SuccessTime desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4625 -@TargetUserName:*$
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count as failures, min(_time) as fail_start, max(_time) as fail_end, values(Authentication.src) as src from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=failure by Authentication.user, Authentication.dest, _time span=1h
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| where failures >= 10
| join type=inner user, dest [| tstats summariesonly=t min(_time) as success_time from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user, Authentication.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`]
| where success_time >= fail_start AND success_time <= fail_end+1800
| sort - success_time
| tstats summariesonly=false count as failures, min(_time) as fail_start, max(_time) as fail_end, values(Authentication.src) as src from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=failure by Authentication.user, Authentication.dest, _time span=1h
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| where failures >= 10
| join type=inner user, dest [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as success_time from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user, Authentication.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`]
| where success_time >= fail_start AND success_time <= fail_end+1800
| sort - success_time
Outbound connection to Kairos data-leak-site backend 62.182.81.38 AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any host reaching the Kairos data-leak-site backend IP (AS30860 / Virtual Systems LLC, Ukraine) confirmed by Cyjax before its SBU seizure. A managed endpoint touching this IP indicates attacker infrastructure contact — staging, exfil handoff, or beaconing tied to the extortion operation. Rationale: 62.182.81.38 is the article's pre-extracted IOC and is independently confirmed by Cyjax as the Kairos leak-site backend (AS30860, Ukraine); an exact-IP network match is inherently low-FP and high-fidelity for attacker-infra contact. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cyjax.com/resources/blog/an-elephant-in-kairos-data-leak-site-emerges-for-new-extortion-group • https://securityaffairs.com/194750/security/u-s-government-agency-paid-1m-to-data-extortion-group-kairos.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst or SOC tooling actively probing/enriching the IP
  • Sandbox or malware-analysis VM detonating Kairos-related samples
  • IP reassigned to a benign tenant after the SBU seizure (validate WHOIS/PTR freshness before escalating)
  • Shared-hosting neighbor service on AS30860 unrelated to Kairos
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process and confirm the IP's current ownership (post-seizure the IP may be reassigned) — a user-context process beaconing to it is high-confidence. 2) Contain: block 62.182.81.38 at the perimeter, isolate the host, and snapshot for forensics. 3) Hunt: correlate the same host/account for temp.sh uploads, large archive staging, and the failed-login burst signature to reconstruct the full theft-extortion chain.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteIP == "62.182.81.38"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DestinationIP == "62.182.81.38"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceAction, SentBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] VS Code / Cursor auto-run task spawns inline node -e / python -c / script host (TaskJacker folderOpen RCE) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BeaverTail loader appends JavaScript to build-config files (postcss/tailwind/next/vite/eslint/babel) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Developer tooling (node) contacts TRON/Aptos/BNB Smart Chain public RPC to stage payload · [LLM] DEV#POPPER stage-2 / socket.io C2 to Evoxt IPs or EmbedIO port 27017
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Scripted Git history rewrite: amend with backdated commit or scripted force-push · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
VS Code / Cursor auto-run task spawns inline node -e / python -c / script host (TaskJacker folderOpen RCE) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the PolinRider/TaskJacker execution trigger where a poisoned .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen makes the IDE silently spawn an interpreter the moment a cloned repo is opened. Scoped to Code.exe/Cursor.exe launching node/python with inline-eval flags or WSH/mshta, which normal IDE terminal usage does not do. Rationale: Uses the article/Socket-confirmed folderOpen tasks.json RCE: IDE (Code.exe/Cursor.exe) auto-spawning an interpreter. The inline-eval/WSH filter separates the malicious loader launch from normal integrated-terminal use, matching eSentire's `node -e <JavaScript>` and `python -c` stager patterns. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/polinrider-north-korea-linked-supply-chain-campaign-expands • https://www.esentire.com/blog/north-korean-apt-malware-analysis-dev-popper-rat-and-omnistealer-everyday-im-shufflin • https://www.scworld.com/news/north-korean-polinrider-supply-chain-attack-targets-108-unique-repos
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1204.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running a legitimate node-based build/test task that uses --eval (rare)
  • VS Code extension that shells out to python -c for tooling
  • Legitimate task automation invoking cscript for a project script
  • Cursor AI agent executing a sanctioned inline node snippet
  • Electron-based tooling packaged under Code.exe naming
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !contains "jest" and ProcessCommandLine !contains "eslint --" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !contains "--extensionTestsPath"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine and decode the inline node/python payload; check the source repo path and whether a .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen exists in that workspace. 2) Contain: isolate the developer host, kill the interpreter tree, and block outbound to blockchain RPC + the DEV#POPPER C2 IPs; treat all secrets on that machine as exposed. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for subsequent node connections to bsc-dataseed.binance.org / trongrid / aptoslabs and modified build-config files (UC2/UC3).

   or (FileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe","python3.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has " -c ")

title: VS Code or Cursor Auto-Run Task Spawns Inline Interpreter (PolinRider TaskJacker)

detection:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\Code.exe OR *\code.exe OR *\Cursor.exe OR *\cursor.exe) (( @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\nodejs.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*\ -e\ * OR *--eval*) ) OR ( @Image:(*\python.exe OR *\pythonw.exe) AND @CommandLine:*\ -c\ * ) OR @Image:(*\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE))

BeaverTail loader appends JavaScript to build-config files (postcss/tailwind/next/vite/eslint/babel) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the PolinRider post-execution behaviour where the loader searches for and appends obfuscated JS to project build-config files so the payload re-executes on the next build/import. Scoped to script interpreters (node/cmd/wscript) modifying these specific config filenames, which a human editor save would not produce. Rationale: Directly uses the article-named files the malware appends JS to (postcss.config.mjs, tailwind.config.js, eslint.config.mjs, next.config.mjs, babel.config.js) plus the .vscode/tasks.json audit target; restricting the writer to interpreters (not editors) is the FP discriminator. Dropped generic app.js/config.js to keep FP tolerable. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/polinrider-north-korea-linked-supply-chain-campaign-expands • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/north-korean-hackers-publish-108.html
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Codegen/scaffolding tools (create-next-app, Nx, Vite) writing config files via node
  • Prettier/ESLint auto-fix rewriting eslint.config.js on save through a node wrapper
  • A build step regenerating tailwind/postcss config
  • Dev running a node script that programmatically edits vite.config.js
  • VS Code extension writing .vscode/tasks.json during project setup
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "create-next-app" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "eslint --fix" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "prettier --write"
Response runbook
1) Triage: diff the config file's last write — look for appended obfuscated JS, long whitespace padding, or references to require('./*.woff2'); confirm the writing process was not a legit scaffolder. 2) Contain: quarantine the repo, revert the config file from a known-good lockfile/commit, and isolate the workstation; rotate secrets from a clean host. 3) Hunt: search the repo tree for fake .woff2 files and for node processes contacting blockchain RPC endpoints (UC3).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated")
| where (FileName in~ ("postcss.config.mjs","tailwind.config.js","eslint.config.mjs","next.config.mjs","babel.config.js","vite.config.js","eslint.config.js"))
   or (FileName =~ "tasks.json" and FolderPath has @"\.vscode\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","nodejs.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","python.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFileName in~ ("postcss.config.mjs","tailwind.config.js","eslint.config.mjs","next.config.mjs","babel.config.js","vite.config.js","eslint.config.js"))
   or (TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json" and TargetFilePath has "\\.vscode\\")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe","\\nodejs.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\python.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

Developer tooling (node) contacts TRON/Aptos/BNB Smart Chain public RPC to stage payload AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the PolinRider second-stage retrieval where the JS loader resolves an encrypted payload via public blockchain RPC (Trongrid, Aptos fullnode, bsc-dataseed / bsc-publicnode) before XOR-decrypting and eval-ing it. Anomalous for a developer workstation node/IDE process outside a genuine web3 project. Rationale: Uses eSentire's confirmed RPC infrastructure (bsc-dataseed.binance.org, bsc-publicnode.com, Trongrid, Aptos fullnode) that the loader queries to resolve the encrypted stage. Restricting to node/IDE/python initiators separates malicious staging from browser-based crypto usage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/north-korean-apt-malware-analysis-dev-popper-rat-and-omnistealer-everyday-im-shufflin • https://cybersecuritynews.com/north-korea-linked-hackers-hide-javascript-loaders/
ATT&CKT1102 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate web3/blockchain developer whose node project queries BSC/TRON/Aptos RPC
  • A crypto-wallet or dApp SDK in an authorized repo
  • Hardhat/Foundry/Truffle test runners hitting public RPC
  • Monitoring/price-feed script polling bsc-dataseed
  • CI agent building a legit DeFi project
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the host's user is a sanctioned blockchain developer and whether the querying node process traces back to a recently cloned repo or an npm postinstall; capture the parent process. 2) Contain: if unsanctioned, isolate the host, block the RPC hosts + DEV#POPPER C2 IPs, and rotate exposed developer/cloud secrets from a clean machine. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC4 (stage-2 C2 on 27017) and UC1/UC2 on the same host to confirm the full chain.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","nodejs.exe","Code.exe","Cursor.exe","python.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("bsc-dataseed.binance.org","bsc-publicnode.com","trongrid.io","aptoslabs.com")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any ("bsc-dataseed.binance.org","bsc-publicnode.com","trongrid.io","aptoslabs.com")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode

DEV#POPPER stage-2 / socket.io C2 to Evoxt IPs or EmbedIO port 27017 AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on the hardcoded DEV#POPPER RAT / OmniStealer C2 infrastructure documented by eSentire: fixed Evoxt-hosted IPs and a stage-2 socket.io/EmbedIO listener on TCP 27017. This is the RAT's live command channel after the blockchain-staged loader executes. Rationale: IPs (136.0.9.8, 23.27.202.27, 198.105.127.210, 23.27.20.143) and the port-27017 EmbedIO/socket.io stage-2 listener are exact eSentire IOCs — hardcoded, high-fidelity. RFC1918 exclusion on the 27017 clause suppresses internal MongoDB. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/north-korean-apt-malware-analysis-dev-popper-rat-and-omnistealer-everyday-im-shufflin
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1571 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node application connecting to an internet-facing MongoDB on 27017 (partly suppressed by RFC1918 filter, external managed Mongo Atlas still possible)
  • Reused/reallocated Evoxt VPS IP later hosting a benign service
  • Security scanner probing 27017 from a node-based tool
  • Legit developer tunnelling to a cloud DB on 27017
Suppression filter
| where not (RemotePort == 27017 and RemoteUrl has_any ("mongodb.net","documents.azure.com"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the RemoteIP hit against the eSentire list; for 27017 hits verify the destination is not a sanctioned MongoDB Atlas/managed cluster and identify the node parent process. 2) Contain: isolate the host immediately, block the four C2 IPs org-wide at the firewall, terminate the node process tree, and force-rotate all credentials/cloud tokens/wallet keys reachable from that host. 3) Hunt: sweep all endpoints for the same IPs/port and for the blockchain-RPC staging (UC3) and folderOpen execution (UC1) to scope the intrusion.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("136.0.9.8","23.27.202.27","198.105.127.210","23.27.20.143")
   or (RemotePort == 27017 and RemoteIPType == "Public" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","nodejs.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("136.0.9.8","23.27.202.27","198.105.127.210","23.27.20.143")
   or (DstPortNumber == 27017 and DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.16.")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction

Scripted Git history rewrite: amend with backdated commit or scripted force-push AIActions on Objectives Low
Hunts the PolinRider anti-forensic tradecraft where a batch/script rewrites the last commit to appear authored by the original maintainer at an older date, then force-pushes. Targets git.exe backdated amends and force-pushes launched by a non-interactive script parent rather than an interactive shell. Rationale: Targets the article's explicit 'Windows batch script to stealthily modify the last commit... appear as if made by the original author' — git commit --amend --date is the backdating tell; scripted (non-interactive) force-push is the covering step. Kept as Low-confidence hunting because force-push alone is common dev behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/north-korean-hackers-publish-108.html • https://socket.dev/blog/polinrider-north-korea-linked-supply-chain-campaign-expands
ATT&CKT1070 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately amending a commit date after a rebase
  • CI/release scripts that force-push tags or squashed branches via node/cmd
  • Git GUI wrappers invoking force-with-lease
  • A monorepo tooling script rewriting history intentionally
  • Interactive rebase workflows that backdate commits
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gitlab-runner","azure-pipelines","jenkins","github-actions"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the git command and the repo — is the amended commit backdated and reattributed to a different author than the console user? Check the parent script/batch file on disk. 2) Contain: preserve the repo reflog and the offending script, freeze pushes to the affected remote, and review recent force-pushed commits for injected loaders/.woff2 files. 3) Hunt: correlate the same host/user with UC1/UC2 (folderOpen execution, config tamper) and package-publish activity to determine if a maintainer account was hijacked.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "git.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "commit" and ProcessCommandLine has "--amend" and ProcessCommandLine has "--date")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "push" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--force"," -f ") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","node.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where (CommandLine has "commit" and CommandLine has "--amend" and CommandLine has "--date")
   or (CommandLine has "push" and CommandLine has_any ("--force"," -f ") and ParentProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\node.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\powershell.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine

  scripted_force_push:
    Image|endswith: '\git.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'push'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--force'
      - ' -f '
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  condition: backdated_amend or scripted_force_push
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\git.exe OR *\Git.exe) ((@CommandLine:*commit* AND @CommandLine:*--amend* AND @CommandLine:*--date*) OR (@CommandLine:*push* AND (@CommandLine:*--force* OR @CommandLine:*\ -f\ *) AND @ParentImage:(*\cmd.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/git\.exe$/i
| (regex("commit", field=CommandLine) AND regex("--amend", field=CommandLine) AND regex("--date", field=CommandLine)) OR (regex("push", field=CommandLine) AND CommandLine=/(--force|\s-f\s)/i AND ParentBaseFileName=/(cmd|node|wscript|cscript|powershell)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="git.exe" AND ((Processes.process="*commit*" AND Processes.process="*--amend*" AND Processes.process="*--date*") OR (Processes.process="*push*" AND (Processes.process="*--force*" OR Processes.process="* -f *") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cmd.exe","node.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="git.exe" AND ((Processes.process="*commit*" AND Processes.process="*--amend*" AND Processes.process="*--date*") OR (Processes.process="*push*" AND (Processes.process="*--force*" OR Processes.process="* -f *") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cmd.exe","node.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")

          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"

          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access

            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

        ParentImage|contains:

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

phpBB CVE-2026-48611 auth bypass: login_link flow forced to 'apache' provider AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact CVE-2026-48611 exploit request against phpBB's ucp.php login-link endpoint where the attacker overrides auth_provider to 'apache' to skip the password check and authenticate as any user. The combination of mode=login_link with auth_provider=apache never occurs in legitimate OAuth account-linking, which only ever uses auth_provider=oauth. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim PoC query string ucp.php?mode=login_link&auth_provider=apache — the auth_provider=apache + mode=login_link pairing is the exploit primitive and never appears in legitimate OAuth account-linking (which only uses auth_provider=oauth). Cross-checked against Pentest-Tools, BleepingComputer, and the phpBB 3.3.17 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized red-team / penetration test replaying CVE-2026-48611 against the forum
  • Automated vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Nuclei, Qualys) that ship a CVE-2026-48611 plugin
  • Bug-bounty researcher validating the patch on a staging phpBB instance
  • Internal QA validating the 3.3.17 fix by re-issuing the malicious request (expect scStatus 4xx post-patch)
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Nuclei","Qualys","zgrab","masscan","Aikido")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm phpBB version (<3.3.17 = vulnerable). Check scStatus — a 302 with Set-Cookie indicates a SUCCESSFUL bypass; 4xx means patched/blocked. Pull the cIP, csUserAgent and the login_username value from the query/body to identify the impersonated account (admin/mod = critical). 2) CONTAIN: If 302 on a vulnerable host, block the source IP at the WAF, force-expire all phpBB sessions (truncate the sessions table / rotate the board's session salt), reset the impersonated account's password, and prioritise upgrade to 3.3.17. 3) HUNT: Search the same cIP for follow-on access to /mcp.php and /adm/index.php (UC2), for PM reads, user/permission changes, or new admin accounts created after the bypass timestamp.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where csUriStem endswith "/ucp.php"
| where csUriQuery contains "mode=login_link"
| where csUriQuery contains "auth_provider=apache"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserName, csUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: phpBB CVE-2026-48611 Authentication Bypass via login_link apache Provider
id: 3f2b1c9a-8d4e-47a6-9c1f-2e7b6a4d0c11
description: Detects the CVE-2026-48611 phpBB authentication bypass where the ucp.php login-link flow is invoked with auth_provider forced to 'apache', skipping the password check to authenticate as any user.

phpBB post-bypass privileged panel access from CVE-2026-48611 source IP AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlates a CVE-2026-48611 bypass request (ucp.php login_link + auth_provider=apache) with subsequent access to the moderator/admin control panels (/mcp.php, /adm/index.php) from the same client IP within one hour, indicating hands-on abuse of the hijacked administrator or moderator session. Rationale: Chains the article's exploit signature (auth_provider=apache login_link) to the privileged endpoints the write-up says the attacker gains control of — moderator/admin panels — using client IP + short temporal window to separate a genuine hijack from background admin-panel noise. Cross-checked against: • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1078 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Forum sits behind a CDN/reverse proxy that collapses all client IPs to the proxy address, so a real admin's /adm/ access falsely correlates with an unrelated scanner's bypass probe (biggest FP — validate against X-Forwarded-For if the logs carry it)
  • Authorized pen-test that both exploits and browses the admin panel from one host (true positive but expected/benign)
  • Shared NAT egress where a legitimate moderator and a scanner exit the same public IP
  • Note: phpBB's ACP (/adm/index.php) enforces a separate password re-auth, so a bypassed session may get 401/redirect there — /mcp.php (moderator panel) has no such re-auth and is the higher-signal path
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the correlated cIP is a real client and not a shared CDN/proxy egress (check whether ALL traffic shows this IP). Review scStatus on the panel requests — 200 on /mcp.php means the hijacked session is actively moderating; a re-auth redirect on /adm/ still leaves board-level admin actions open. 2) CONTAIN: Invalidate all phpBB sessions (rotate session salt / truncate sessions), reset the affected admin/mod passwords, block the source IP, and upgrade to 3.3.17. 3) HUNT: Enumerate what the session touched after the bypass — user/permission edits, new admin accounts, group changes, bulk PM reads, board config or ext installs; diff the users and acl tables against a known-good backup.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-6682", "CVE-2026-6687", "CVE-2026-6688", "CVE-2026-6685", "CVE-2026-6683", "CVE-2026-6686", "CVE-2026-6684")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-6682", "CVE-2026-6687", "CVE-2026-6688", "CVE-2026-6685", "CVE-2026-6683", "CVE-2026-6686", "CVE-2026-6684")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-6682", "CVE-2026-6687", "CVE-2026-6688", "CVE-2026-6685", "CVE-2026-6683", "CVE-2026-6686", "CVE-2026-6684")

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores

status: experimental
description: |
