ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46242", "CVE-2026-43074", "CVE-2026-31431", "CVE-2026-31694", "CVE-2026-4747")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46242", "CVE-2026-43074", "CVE-2026-31431", "CVE-2026-31694", "CVE-2026-4747")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New Avalon Malware Framework Packs CrownX Ransomware Capabilities

The Hacker News
2026-07-03 20 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a previously undocumented modular malware framework codenamed Avalon that's distributed by means of a multi-stage phishing chain capable of bypassing traditional security controls. Avalon combines credential collection, lateral movement, remote access, recovery disruption, and ransomware execution, bringing together diverse functions under one

ATT&CKT1021.001 T1190 T1486 T1555.003 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Avalon/CrownX delivery-chain file & payload hash sweep (ISO, LNK, MSBuild loader, CrownX) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] LNK-launched MSBuild executing non-standard project from Temp (Avalon CodeTaskFactory in-memory loader) · Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] MSBuild.exe outbound HTTPS to public IP (Avalon in-memory downloader fetching next stage) · [LLM] Avalon C2 to helloxcherry.com / 45.131.66.106 / 64.20.53.230 (/api/v2/tasking, X-Edge-Cache beacon) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] CrownX ransomware mass file encryption - .8hn2yc extension (Data Encrypted for Impact) · [LLM] CrownX anti-forensic recovery/artifact destruction (VSS + Prefetch/AmCache/SRUM/BAM + PhysicalDrive) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Avalon/CrownX delivery-chain file & payload hash sweep (ISO, LNK, MSBuild loader, CrownX) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the five corroborated Avalon SHA256 artifacts (ISO, LNK, MSBuild inline-task project, in-memory loader, final CrownX payload) as they are dropped or executed. Highest-confidence, lowest-effort retro-sweep for the specific Blackpoint-documented campaign. Rationale: All five SHA256 (ISO b7d5.., LNK 607c.., MSBuild project 59a2.., loader 4b73.., payload c725..) are published in Blackpoint's IOC table and echoed by cyberpress/gbhackers; a hash match is unambiguous. Cross-checked Blackpoint blog + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://blackpointcyber.com/blog/avalons-path-from-legal-lure-to-crownx-ransom-capabilities/ • https://cyberpress.org/crownx-ransomware-attack/ • https://gbhackers.com/crownx-ransomware-capabilities/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1566.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / malware analyst detonating the sample in a lab VM that reports to the same tenant
  • Threat-intel sandbox or CI malware-scanning host executing submitted files
  • IR team copying the artifact onto a forensic workstation for analysis
  • AV/EDR quarantine copy retaining the file hash under a vault path
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "\\AV_Quarantine\\" and DeviceName !in~ ("MALWARE-LAB01","IR-FORENSIC01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the matched hash and host; check whether the file is in a live user path (Downloads/Temp/mounted ISO) vs an analyst/quarantine path. 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, kill any msbuild.exe/loader process, block helloxcherry.com and 45.131.66.106 / 64.20.53.230 at the egress proxy/firewall. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the other four hashes, the .8hn2yc extension, and outbound to helloxcherry.com to scope lateral spread to Veeam/vCenter/Hyper-V assets.
let AvalonHashes = dynamic(["b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28","607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6","59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a","4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba","c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3"]);
union
  (DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (AvalonHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, Source="FileEvent", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (AvalonHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, Source="ProcessEvent", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let AvalonHashes = dynamic(["b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28","607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6","59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a","4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba","c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 in (AvalonHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Avalon/CrownX Known Malicious File Hash Observed
id: 8f2a1c47-3b9e-4d21-9a6f-1e77c0a4b512
description: Detects any of the five Blackpoint-documented Avalon/CrownX SHA256 artifacts written to disk.

LNK-launched MSBuild executing non-standard project from Temp (Avalon CodeTaskFactory in-memory loader) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Avalon execution primitive: a document LNK spawns cmd.exe (delayed-expansion drive search) which copies an MSBuild project to %TEMP% and runs it via the .NET Framework MSBuild.exe, using CodeTaskFactory inline C# to rebuild a downloader in memory. Flags MSBuild consuming a .tmp/.dat project from Temp under cmd.exe/explorer — not a normal build pattern. Rationale: Blackpoint documents the exact chain: LNK -> cmd.exe (delayed expansion, drive-letter search) -> copy MSBuild project (zfighv.tmp) to %TEMP%\ngen0cc9.dat -> MSBuild.exe CodeTaskFactory. MSBuild consuming a .tmp/.dat from Temp under cmd.exe is a rare, high-fidelity LOLBin pattern. Corroborated Blackpoint blog + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://blackpointcyber.com/blog/avalons-path-from-legal-lure-to-crownx-ransom-capabilities/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-avalon-malware-framework-packs.html
ATT&CKT1127.001 T1620 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or build engineer invoking MSBuild manually from a cmd prompt against a project temporarily in %TEMP%
  • CI/CD agent that stages generated .tmp build files in Temp before compiling
  • Installer/packaging tool that compiles inline MSBuild tasks at setup time
  • Visual Studio generating and building intermediate project files under a Temp path
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("devenv.exe","msbuild.exe","dotnet.exe","vs_installer.exe") or GrandParent in~ ("devenv.exe","dotnet.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full MSBuild command line and grandparent (expect explorer.exe from an LNK on a mounted ISO drive letter); confirm the project file is a .tmp/.dat, not a real .csproj/.sln. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill msbuild.exe and any child, capture %TEMP%\ngen0cc9.dat and the mounted ISO for forensics. 3) Hunt: check DeviceNetworkEvents for msbuild.exe/loader reaching helloxcherry.com or 45.131.66.106/64.20.53.230, and search EmailEvents/UrlClickEvents for the Proton Drive legal-lure that delivered the ISO.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "msbuild.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","explorer.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp", ".tmp", ".dat", "ngen0cc9.dat", "zfighv.tmp", "Mimecast Secure File Logs")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProc = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          MSBuildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\MSBuild.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\cmd.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\Temp\", ".tmp", ".dat", "ngen0cc9.dat", "zfighv.tmp", "Mimecast Secure File Logs")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 2d4c9a11-77f0-4e63-8b2a-9c1d5e0f3a88

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\MSBuild.exe OR *\\msbuild.exe OR *\\MSBUILD.EXE) @ParentImage:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\explorer.exe OR *\\EXPLORER.EXE) @CommandLine:(*\\Temp\\* OR *.tmp* OR *.dat* OR *ngen0cc9.dat* OR *zfighv.tmp*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\MSBuild\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/(cmd|explorer)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\\\Temp\\\\|\.tmp|\.dat|ngen0cc9\.dat|zfighv\.tmp)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count(as=cnt))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="msbuild.exe" AND (Processes.parent_process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe") AND (Processes.process="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process="*.tmp*" OR Processes.process="*.dat*" OR Processes.process="*ngen0cc9.dat*" OR Processes.process="*zfighv.tmp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="msbuild.exe" AND (Processes.parent_process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe") AND (Processes.process="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process="*.tmp*" OR Processes.process="*.dat*" OR Processes.process="*ngen0cc9.dat*" OR Processes.process="*zfighv.tmp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
MSBuild.exe outbound HTTPS to public IP (Avalon in-memory downloader fetching next stage) AICommand & Control High
Hunts MSBuild.exe (a build tool with no legitimate reason to egress to the internet) making an outbound connection to a public address, matching Avalon's managed downloader that patches ETW/AMSI then fetches the next stage over HTTPS via WinHTTP. Rationale: MSBuild.exe egressing to a public IP has effectively zero benign cause on endpoints; Blackpoint confirms the managed downloader (loaded by MSBuild's CodeTaskFactory task) fetches the next stage over HTTPS. Process pivot survives C2 domain/IP rotation. Sentinel left empty: this tenant has no process-attributed network table (DeviceNetworkEvents/Sysmon EID3 not in the Sentinel schema set); the domain/IP IOC is covered by the Avalon C2 UC. Corroborated Blackpoint blog. Cross-checked against: • https://blackpointcyber.com/blog/avalons-path-from-legal-lure-to-crownx-ransom-capabilities/
ATT&CKT1127.001 T1105 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MSBuild NuGet/package restore pulling dependencies from a public feed (nuget.org) during a legit build on a developer/build host
  • MSBuild task that legitimately downloads SDK components or symbols
  • Build agent behind no proxy reaching public artifact repositories
  • Telemetry/crash-reporting task compiled into a build step
Suppression filter
| where RemoteUrl !has "nuget.org" and DeviceName !in~ ("BUILD-AGENT01","DEV-CI01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve the RemoteIP/RemoteUrl and check whether the parent chain is the Avalon LNK->cmd->MSBuild loader (Temp .tmp/.dat project) vs a real build host/CI agent. 2) Contain: isolate host, block the destination IP/domain at egress, kill msbuild.exe. 3) Hunt: pull the fetched next-stage payload (hash against c725815c..), and check the same host for .8hn2yc file creation and shadow-copy/forensic-store deletion indicating CrownX detonation.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "msbuild.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "msbuild.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by TimeGenerated desc

#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\MSBuild\.exe$/i ConnectionDirection="1"

| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)

NETWORK

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app="msbuild.exe" AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app="msbuild.exe" AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Avalon C2 to helloxcherry.com / 45.131.66.106 / 64.20.53.230 (/api/v2/tasking, X-Edge-Cache beacon) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts direct network/DNS contact with the Avalon C2 infrastructure — domain helloxcherry.com, staging IPs, the /api/v2/tasking WinHTTP POST endpoint, and the /cdn/static/<md5>/update staging path — regardless of which process beacons. Catches later-stage Avalon C2 that no longer runs under MSBuild. Rationale: helloxcherry.com plus the /api/v2/tasking WinHTTP POST endpoint and /cdn/static/<md5>/update staging path are published in Blackpoint's IOC section and echoed in The Hacker News; the two IPs are the pre-extracted campaign IPs. Any resolution/connection is high-fidelity. Corroborated Blackpoint blog + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://blackpointcyber.com/blog/avalons-path-from-legal-lure-to-crownx-ransom-capabilities/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-avalon-malware-framework-packs.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security proxy/sandbox detonation or TI enrichment service resolving the IOC domain for analysis
  • Blocklist/threat-feed validation tooling that actively probes known-bad domains
  • Analyst manually browsing the IOC in a triage VM
  • Passive-DNS or brand-monitoring appliance querying the domain
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and DeviceName !in~ ("TI-SANDBOX01","PROXY-DETONATE01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process (InitiatingProcessFileName/ContextImageFileName) and whether the endpoint is a user host vs a known TI/proxy sandbox. 2) Contain: sinkhole/block helloxcherry.com and 45.131.66.106 / 64.20.53.230 tenant-wide, isolate the beaconing host. 3) Hunt: on the host, review WinHTTP POSTs to /api/v2/tasking (LSASS/SAM form-field exfil), pull the /cdn/static staging download, and check for CrownX detonation (.8hn2yc, shadow-copy deletion).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "helloxcherry.com"
    or RemoteUrl has "/api/v2/tasking"
    or RemoteIP in ("45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has "helloxcherry.com" | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname, Indicator=DnsQuery, Kind="DNS"),
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr in ("45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230") or Url has_any ("helloxcherry.com","/api/v2/tasking") | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname, Indicator=strcat(DstIpAddr, " ", Url), Kind="NetSession"),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationDnsDomain has "helloxcherry.com" or DestinationIP in ("45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230") or RequestURL has_any ("helloxcherry.com","/api/v2/tasking") | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, DvcHostname=DvcHostname, Indicator=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationIP), Kind="Proxy/FW")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230") OR All_Traffic.dest="helloxcherry.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="helloxcherry.com" OR DNS.query="*.helloxcherry.com" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`

CrownX ransomware mass file encryption - .8hn2yc extension (Data Encrypted for Impact) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts CrownX file encryption by its unique appended extension .8hn2yc across engineering (.blend/.sldprt), business, database and VM-image (.vmdk/.vhdx/.qcow2) files, thresholded per host to flag a mass-rename burst. Rationale: Blackpoint's IOC table gives the exact CrownX encrypted-file extension .8hn2yc (random per-campaign string, no benign use). Single-event Sigma catches any occurrence; the KQL/SPL threshold of 25/10min confirms a mass-encryption burst while suppressing an isolated coincidental match. Corroborated Blackpoint blog. Cross-checked against: • https://blackpointcyber.com/blog/avalons-path-from-legal-lure-to-crownx-ransom-capabilities/
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Extremely unlikely benign match - .8hn2yc is a random 6-char string; a user file coincidentally named *.8hn2yc
  • Backup/replication job copying already-encrypted victim files across shares (secondary spread of true positives, not a real FP)
  • EDR/forensic tooling re-writing sample encrypted files during analysis
  • Restore test replaying encrypted files into a lab
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the encrypting process (InitiatingProcessFileName/ActingProcessName) and the burst host; confirm ransom note presence and deadline-timer note. 2) Contain: immediately network-isolate all hosts showing .8hn2yc writes, disable the actor account, kill the encryptor, and freeze Veeam/Acronis/vCenter/Hyper-V backup assets from being reached. 3) Hunt: fleet-sweep for .8hn2yc, shadow-copy/forensic-store deletion, and helloxcherry.com C2 to find every encrypted host and the lateral-movement path before restoring from offline backups.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".8hn2yc"
| summarize EncryptedFiles = count(),
            SampleFile = any(FolderPath),
            Actor = any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            ActorCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where EncryptedFiles > 25
| order by EncryptedFiles desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".8hn2yc"
| summarize EncryptedFiles = count(), SampleFile = any(TargetFilePath), Actor = any(ActingProcessName)
          by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where EncryptedFiles > 25
| order by EncryptedFiles desc

CrownX anti-forensic recovery/artifact destruction (VSS + Prefetch/AmCache/SRUM/BAM + PhysicalDrive) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts CrownX's recovery-inhibition and anti-forensic subsystem: deletion of Windows forensic stores (Prefetch, AmCache, SRUM, BAM/DAM, PowerShell history), WinRE/System-Restore wiping, and direct \\.\PhysicalDrive raw-disk access. Distinct from a generic vssadmin rule by pivoting on the forensic-store/raw-disk targets Blackpoint enumerated. Rationale: Blackpoint explicitly lists CrownX's anti-forensic targets: VSS, WinRE, System Restore, Prefetch, AmCache, SRUM, BAM, DAM, ShimCache, PowerShell history, and \\.\PhysicalDrive%d direct disk access. Deleting these forensic stores in a tight burst (plus raw-disk/reagentc/vssadmin signals) is a strong ransomware-impact indicator that a lone vssadmin rule misses. Sigma skipped: this UC is a threshold + cross-signal correlation, not single-event shape. Corroborated Blackpoint blog. Cross-checked against: • https://blackpointcyber.com/blog/avalons-path-from-legal-lure-to-crownx-ransom-capabilities/
ATT&CKT1490 T1070.004 T1561.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Disk-cleanup / privacy tools (CCleaner, BleachBit) purging Prefetch and PowerShell history
  • SysAdmin running reagentc /disable during WinRE servicing or imaging
  • Legit ransomware-hardening scripts that pre-emptively clear SRUM/BAM during forensic-readiness testing
  • Backup software pruning VSS snapshots as part of retention
  • OS reset / re-imaging workflow that wipes Amcache/Prefetch
Suppression filter
| where Actor !in~ ("ccleaner.exe","bleachbit.exe","cleanmgr.exe","dism.exe") and Actor !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the process doing the burst deletions (InitiatingProcessId/ContextImageFileName) and whether \\.\PhysicalDrive or reagentc /disable co-occurred on the host; correlate to any .8hn2yc writes. 2) Contain: isolate the host immediately (raw-disk access can brick boot records), suspend the actor account, and snapshot/preserve any remaining VSS from a hypervisor level if virtual. 3) Hunt: check for the MSBuild loader chain and helloxcherry.com C2 on the same host, and sweep backup/virtualization assets (Veeam/Acronis/vCenter/Hyper-V) for the same deletion pattern indicating recovery-platform targeting.
let ForensicDeletes = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "FileDeleted"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Windows\Prefetch\", @"\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve", @"\System32\sru\", @"\System32\LogFiles\Sum\", "ConsoleHost_history.txt")
    | summarize DeleteCount = count(), Targets = make_set(FolderPath, 20), Actor = any(InitiatingProcessFileName)
              by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
    | where DeleteCount > 3;
let RawDiskOrRecovery = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has @"\\.\PhysicalDrive"
        or (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "disable")
        or (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete shadows")
        or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadowcopy","delete"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RawSignal = ProcessCommandLine, Actor2 = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ForensicDeletes
| join kind=leftouter (RawDiskOrRecovery | summarize RawSignals = make_set(RawSignal, 10) by DeviceName) on DeviceName
| project DeviceName, Timestamp, DeleteCount, Targets, Actor, RawSignals
| order by DeleteCount desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType == "FileDeleted"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Windows\Prefetch\", @"\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve", @"\System32\sru\", @"\System32\LogFiles\Sum\", "ConsoleHost_history.txt")
| summarize DeleteCount = count(), Targets = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Actor = any(ActingProcessName)
          by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where DeleteCount > 3
| order by DeleteCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @EventType:(Delete OR DeletedExecutable) @TargetFilename:(*\\Windows\\Prefetch\\* OR *\\Amcache.hve* OR *\\System32\\sru\\* OR *ConsoleHost_history.txt*)
#event_simpleName=FileDeleted TargetFileName=/(\\Windows\\Prefetch\\|Amcache\.hve|\\System32\\sru\\|ConsoleHost_history\.txt)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=DeleteCount))
| DeleteCount > 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Filesystem.file_path) as targets min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="deleted" AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\Prefetch\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppCompat\\Programs\\Amcache.hve*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\sru\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*ConsoleHost_history.txt*") by Filesystem.dest span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as targets min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="deleted" AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\Prefetch\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppCompat\\Programs\\Amcache.hve*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\sru\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*ConsoleHost_history.txt*") by Filesystem.dest span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser

level: high

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-3248", "CVE-2021-29441")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-3248", "CVE-2021-29441")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07

description: |

references:

date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    category: process_creation

detection:

            - '\excel.exe'

            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution

status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

logsource:

            - '\psexec.exe'

            - '\psexesvc.exe'

            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

        Image|endswith:

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3") or SHA1 in~ ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3") or MD5 in~ ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3") or SHA1 in~ ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3") or MD5 in~ ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("b7d50d0406afcd2efd87bf3bf8c4211719ba9817dd2e0ad62af10c933e765e28", "607cb58b8a592885eef5cfbe35ddce962741b0775c575f58cb3a96ca0ee893a6", "59a260716d05c20229c6a46fe0a2fb5b80fa30c9c73a850222d9d3454426a60a", "4b7301f02b8312ae6de614981f325dbbabee32166630618fdff74615d9a487ba", "c725815cbb07ab5be8903e74ef8aea46ef9c25e4a3bc626ae94bfc1ae21df6e3")
